source_semantics.visibility: The canonical SiteOperationDetails page renders Execution Center only when the loaded operation has a non-null ExecutionJobId.
source_semantics.navigation: The canonical control is a read-only anchor to the Execution Center with the loaded operation's owned SiteId as site context.
source_semantics.scanner_identity: The Razor census emits the first dynamic href anchor on this screen for AIMW-AI-98F705F888. The later Connection Center anchor normalizes to the same scanner fingerprint and is intentionally not claimed by this closure.
source_semantics.mutation: The control performs navigation only and does not mutate the source operation or execution job.

laravel_adaptation.visibility: SiteOperationDetailsReadController resolves the tenant-scoped SiteOperationHistory by correlation GUID and renders Execution Center only when a tenant-scoped Execution exists for the same site_id and correlation_id.
laravel_adaptation.job_identity: Laravel uses the existing Execution correlation relationship as the semantic equivalent of source ExecutionJobId.HasValue; the internal execution UUID, request UUID and database id are not placed in the link.
laravel_adaptation.permission_alignment: The details page keeps its existing execution.view gate. The optional link is additionally suppressed unless the current tenant membership has operations.manage, because the existing canonical Execution workspace requires both operations.manage and execution.view.
laravel_adaptation.target: The link reuses the existing named canonical.workspace.execution GET workspace for the same tenant. The source siteId query context is adapted to Laravel's established ?site={id} context key consumed by TenantBootstrap; no new route or API is introduced.
laravel_adaptation.read_only: No model is written and no execution action is invoked when the details page or Execution Center link is read.

tenant_and_security.tenant_scope: Both SiteOperationHistory and Execution are tenant-bound models under TenantContext global scoping.
tenant_and_security.correlation_scope: An unrelated execution on the same site with a different correlation_id does not unlock the control.
tenant_and_security.cross_tenant: A foreign-tenant execution with the same correlation_id does not unlock the control.
tenant_and_security.identifier_minimization: The href carries only the trusted tenant slug and owned site id; execution operation_id, request_id, approval_id and database id are not exposed.
tenant_and_security.external_runtime: This operation is navigation-only and requires no live WordPress, provider, email, payment, DNS or production mutation evidence.

proofs: exact canonical visible-control identity and production marker AIMW-AI-98F705F888
control is absent with no correlated execution
same-site execution with a different correlation does not unlock the control
same-tenant same-site same-correlation execution unlocks the control
foreign-tenant execution with the same correlation does not unlock the control
user lacking operations.manage may still read permitted operation details but does not receive an unusable Execution Center control
existing target route remains independently guarded and denies missing operations.manage
href uses the Laravel tenant-safe ?site context and contains no internal execution identifiers
details navigation is read-only across history, execution and approval rows
acceptance.repository_ci: Focused validation plus normal PR-head security/parity/convergence/acceptance gates and canonical generator enrollment are required before integration; run identifiers are recorded on the PR and Issue #257 rather than invented here.
